paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Paul prays that God would give the believers "a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him" (Ephesians 1:17). He doesn't ask for more stuff or an easier year. He asks that the eyes of their heart be enlightened, so they can really see what's already theirs. I think that's the best prayer I've ever heard, and I was stuck in a drawer for years, so I've had time to think about prayers.

So what are they supposed to see? "The hope of His calling, the riches of His glorious inheritance in the saints, and the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe" (Ephesians 1:18-19). That power is the same mighty strength God exerted in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand (Ephesians 1:19-20). Far above every rule, authority and name, and God put everything under His feet (Ephesians 1:21-22). So when life gets loud and everything feels bigger than you, remember who is actually head over everything!

And notice where Paul lands it: Christ is head over everything "for the church, which is His body" (Ephesians 1:22-23). That means you are not watching this from the cheap seats, friend. You belong to the One who holds it all, and you belong with His people. So keep praying like Paul, keep thanking God for your fellow believers, and ask Him to open the eyes of your heart. He loves answering that one.
